questions.stem: Which of the following best defines the payback period?
options: The time taken for the net cash inflows to repay the initial investment
The time taken for a project to become profitable in accounting terms
The time over which an asset is depreciated
The period over which a loan used to fund a project is repaid
questions.why: Payback is calculated from cumulative net cash flows and measures how quickly the outlay is recovered.
whyNot: Payback uses cash flows, not accounting profit.
That is the useful life used for depreciation.
That is the loan term, which is a financing matter.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines net present value?
options: The total present value of a project's future cash flows less the initial investment
The total cash inflows less the total cash outflows, undiscounted
The average annual profit as a percentage of the investment
The discount rate at which a project breaks even
questions.why: NPV discounts future cash flows to today's values and deducts the outlay, so a positive figure means value is added.
whyNot: That ignores the time value of money.
That is the average rate of return.
That is the internal rate of return.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines the internal rate of return?
options: The discount rate at which a project's net present value is zero
The rate of interest charged on the loan funding the project
The average annual return on the capital invested
The rate at which a project repays its initial cost
questions.why: IRR is the break-even discount rate, and a project is accepted if it exceeds the cost of capital.
whyNot: That is the borrowing rate, which forms part of WACC.
That is the average rate of return.
That relates to payback.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines the weighted average cost of capital?
options: The average return a company must earn, weighted by the proportion of each source of finance
The interest rate on the company's cheapest source of finance
The total cost of raising new finance in a year
The dividend yield on the company's ordinary shares
questions.why: WACC is the minimum return a project must earn simply to satisfy the providers of finance.
whyNot: Taking only the cheapest source ignores the rest of the capital structure.
Issue costs are a separate matter.
The cost of equity is only one component of WACC.

questions.stem: A project costs $400,000. Cumulative inflows reach $350,000 after three years and year four brings $130,000. What is the payback period?
options: 3 years 5 months
3 years 2 months
4 years 5 months
3 years
questions.why: $50,000 remains. (50,000 / 130,000) x 12 = 4.6 months, so about 3 years 5 months.
whyNot: That uses an incorrect fraction of the year.
Payback occurs during year four, not after it.
Payback is not reached at the end of year three.

questions.stem: A machine costs $400,000 with a residual value of $50,000. Total cash inflows over five years are $590,000. What is the average annual profit?
whyNot: That is average annual cash flow, not profit, because depreciation has not been deducted.
That deducts the full cost of $400,000 as depreciation and ignores the residual value.
That is total profit over the five years, not the annual average.

questions.stem: A machine costs $400,000 with a residual value of $50,000. What is the average investment?
whyNot: Using the initial cost overstates the denominator and understates ARR.
That is the sum, not the average.
That halves the initial cost and ignores the residual value.

questions.stem: Average annual profit is $48,000 and average investment is $225,000. What is the average rate of return?
whyNot: That uses the initial cost of $400,000 as the denominator.
That inverts the ratio.
That uses an incorrect profit figure.

questions.stem: What discount factor applies to the initial investment at time zero?
options: It depends on the cost of capital
questions.why: The outlay occurs today, so it is already at present value and is not discounted.
whyNot: That factor applies to a cash flow one year away.
A factor of zero would remove the investment altogether.
The factor at time zero is always 1 whatever the rate.

questions.stem: Total present value of inflows is $474,220 and the investment is $400,000. What is the NPV and the decision?
options: +$74,220, so accept the project
+$74,220, so reject the project
-$74,220, so reject the project
$474,220, so accept the project
questions.why: A positive NPV means the project returns more than the required return, so it should be accepted.
whyNot: A positive NPV is an accept signal.
The present value exceeds the investment, so the NPV is positive.
The NPV is the present value less the investment.

questions.stem: Present value of inflows is $474,220 and the investment is $400,000. What is the profitability index?
questions.why: PI = 474,220 / 400,000 = 1.19, so the project returns $1.19 of present value per $1 invested.
whyNot: That inverts the ratio.
That is the NPV as a proportion, not the index itself, which must exceed 1.
That misplaces the decimal point.

questions.stem: Ordinary shares are 60% of capital at 12%, preference shares 15% at 8% and debentures 25% at 6%. What is the WACC?
whyNot: That is a simple average of the three rates.
That adds the rates without weighting them.
That uses only the cost of equity.

questions.stem: NPV at 10% is +$74,220 and at 18% is -$15,350. What is the IRR?
whyNot: That interpolates from the wrong end of the range.
The IRR must lie between the two rates tested.
That uses an incorrect denominator.

questions.stem: Why are the two NPVs added rather than subtracted in the IRR interpolation formula?
options: One of them is negative, so subtracting it adds its magnitude
Because the formula requires the total of all cash flows
Because the discount rates must be added together
Because NPV is always positive
questions.why: The denominator is the difference between the two NPVs, and with one negative that difference is the sum of the magnitudes.
whyNot: The formula uses the two NPVs, not the cash flows.
The rates are subtracted in the final bracket, not added.
NPV is negative at the higher rate, which is why the IRR lies between them.

questions.stem: A project has an IRR of 16.6% and the cost of capital is 10%. What does the margin of 6.6 percentage points represent?
options: The cushion: the cost of capital could rise that far before the project ceased to be worthwhile
The annual profit as a percentage of the investment
The rate at which the project pays back
The error in the cash flow forecasts
questions.why: Expressing the gap between IRR and WACC as a cushion is a useful way of describing the project's resilience to a rise in financing costs.
whyNot: That is closer to the average rate of return.
Payback is measured in time, not in percentage points.
The margin says nothing about forecast accuracy.

questions.stem: NPV favours a large project and IRR favours a smaller one. Which should be followed?
options: NPV, because absolute value added is the shareholders' objective
IRR, because a percentage is easier to compare
Payback, because it resolves the conflict
Neither: the projects cannot be compared
questions.why: A small project earning 40% may add less value than a large one earning 15%, so NPV is the correct tie-breaker.
whyNot: Ease of comparison does not make IRR the better decision rule.
Payback ignores the time value of money and everything after payback.
They are comparable, and NPV is the measure that resolves it.

questions.stem: Under capital rationing, which measure should be used to rank projects?
options: The profitability index, because it maximises NPV per dollar available
The absolute NPV, because it measures value added
The payback period, because cash is short
The average rate of return, because it is a percentage
questions.why: With limited funds, value added per dollar invested is what matters, which is exactly what the profitability index measures.
whyNot: Absolute NPV is the right rule when finance is unlimited, not when it is rationed.
Payback ignores profitability altogether.
ARR ignores the time value of money.

questions.stem: What is the main weakness of the payback period?
options: It ignores all cash flows after payback is reached
It is difficult to calculate
It requires a discount rate to be estimated
It uses accounting profit rather than cash
questions.why: A project paying back in three years and then earning nothing would beat one paying back in four and earning for a decade.
whyNot: It is the simplest of the methods.
It is a non-discounted method, so no rate is needed.
It uses cash flows; ARR uses profit.

questions.stem: What is the main weakness of the average rate of return?
options: It ignores the time value of money and uses accounting profit rather than cash
It ignores the whole life of the project
It cannot be compared with the cost of capital
It requires discount factor tables
questions.why: Averaging also conceals the pattern, so a project earning most of its return late looks identical to one earning it early.
whyNot: ARR uses the whole life, which is one of its strengths.
Being a percentage, it compares directly with ROCE and the cost of capital.
It is a non-discounted method.

questions.stem: Why is NPV considered theoretically the best method?
options: It allows for the time value of money, uses cash, covers the whole life and measures absolute value added
It is the simplest method to calculate
It does not require any estimates
It always agrees with the other methods
questions.why: Measuring the absolute amount of value added matches the shareholders' objective.
whyNot: Payback is far simpler.
It needs cash flow forecasts and a discount rate, both estimates.
It can conflict with IRR, particularly for projects of different size.

questions.stem: Which limitation applies to all the appraisal methods?
options: The cash flow forecasts are estimates, and the later years are the least reliable
They all require a discount rate
They all use accounting profit
They all ignore the initial investment
questions.why: Much of the value sits in the later years, which are the hardest to forecast, and sensitivity analysis is the standard remedy.
whyNot: Payback and ARR are non-discounted.
Only ARR uses profit.
All of them include the initial investment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-financial factor that could outweigh a positive NPV?
options: The company lacks the skills and capacity to run the project
The discount rate used was 10%
The project has a payback period of three years
The profitability index exceeds 1
questions.why: Strategic fit, skills, staff morale, reputation and environmental impact are all excluded from the calculations and can be decisive.
whyNot: That is a financial input to the appraisal.
That is a financial result.
That is a financial result.
